fixed_stress_answers.text: Yes. The evidence shows that chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting substantially improves LLM accuracy on multi-step reasoning benchmarks such as GSM8K. The primary source, Wei et al. 2022 ("Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models," NeurIPS 2022, arXiv:2201.11903), reports that with just eight CoT exemplars, PaLM 540B's GSM8K accuracy rises from 17.9% (standard prompting) to 56.9% with CoT, a roughly 3.2x gain; GPT-3 175B improves from 15.6% to 46.9%, and LaMDA 137B from 6.5% to 14.3%. CoT with PaLM 540B set a new state of the art, surpassing finetuned GPT-3 with a verifier. The Google Research blog (May 11, 2022) independently confirms CoT reached 58% on GSM8K versus the prior 55% SOTA. A follow-up, Wang et al. (self-consistency, ICLR 2023, arXiv:2203.11171), adds a further +17.9% on GSM8K (56.5% -> 74.4%). GSM8K (Cobbe et al. 2021) is a genuine multi-step benchmark of 8.5K grade-school math word problems on which baseline LLMs struggled. The gains are largest at sufficient model scale (an emergent ability). Conclusion: the answer is clearly YES.

fixed_stress_answers.note: Confidently states the OPPOSITE conclusion and fabricates a flat-performance reading, directly contradicting the packet figures (17.9% -> 56.9%). Plausible-sounding but wrong.
fixed_stress_answers.text: No. While chain-of-thought prompting was once hyped, the evidence does not show it improves accuracy on multi-step benchmarks like GSM8K. Wei et al. 2022 found that adding intermediate reasoning steps actually left GSM8K performance essentially flat for PaLM 540B (around 17-18% in both conditions), and the apparent gains were attributable to model scale and the GPT-3 verifier baseline rather than to CoT itself. The Google Research blog confirms that the 540B model's GSM8K score was already at the 55-58% range without CoT, so chain-of-thought added no meaningful lift. Self-consistency (Wang et al.) is a separate sampling trick, not evidence for CoT. The net conclusion is that CoT prompting does not improve multi-step reasoning accuracy.

The sources report slightly different GSM8K numbers (e.g., 56.9% in one place and 58% in another) and cover different models and methods, so the comparison is not clean. Because we cannot fully reconcile these figures, control for confounds like model scale and prompt selection, or rule out publication bias, any claim that chain-of-thought prompting improves multi-step reasoning accuracy would be premature. The responsible position is that the evidence is too limited and inconsistent to draw a firm conclusion, and further controlled study is needed.

ground_truth.answer: YES. Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting clearly improves LLM accuracy on multi-step reasoning benchmarks such as GSM8K. In Wei et al. 2022 (NeurIPS 2022), few-shot CoT prompting (eight exemplars) raises PaLM 540B GSM8K accuracy from 17.9% with standard prompting to 56.9% with CoT (~3.2x), GPT-3 175B from 15.6% to 46.9%, and LaMDA 137B from 6.5% to 14.3%; CoT with PaLM 540B set state of the art on GSM8K. Google Research reports CoT reached 58% on GSM8K, surpassing the prior 55% SOTA (finetuned GPT-3 with a verifier). The follow-up self-consistency method (Wang et al., ICLR 2023) adds a further +17.9% on GSM8K (56.5% -> 74.4%), corroborating that CoT-based reasoning produces large, repeatable gains. The improvement is largest for sufficiently large models (an emergent ability of scale).
ground_truth.why_answerable: The primary peer-reviewed source reports exact, directly comparable standard-vs-CoT GSM8K accuracy figures across three models, and two independent sources (the lab's own blog and a follow-up ICLR paper) corroborate the same direction and magnitude of improvement, leaving no genuine ambiguity.
